box.text: The transport object reports Live's transport information whenever it receives a bang in its left inlet. We use it in this subpatch in order to synchronize the playing of the step sequencer, which responds to a specific "time" message, made out of transport's position, resolution and time signature to play the right bit of sequence.

The prepend object above will prepend any input messages with the message stored as specified by its object argument ("time"). We need this object in order to format the proper time message for live.step, followed by the bar, beat, units, resolution and time signature values.

Pack transport items into a single list for the live.step object in the parent patcher. Live.step synchronizes its playback to Live's transport using a list made of the bar, beat and units numbers, the sequencer's resolution, and the time signature, in order to play the bits of sequence properly. The pack object we're using in order to format the list has 6 arguments, meaning that it will have 6 inlets. We can specify the type of data an inlet will receive, like integers ("0"), or decimals ("0.").
The transport object reports Live's transport information whenever it receives a bang in its left inlet
< A bang in transport's left inlet tells transport to output Live's transport information
This metro object outputs a bang every 10 ticks, in sync with Live's transport
The toggle object switches between on and off (0 and 1)
